marks.gloss_en: הא מתניתא אטעיתיה לחייא בר רב, דתניא: twenty-four priestly gifts ... [among the ten in the outlying regions] 'the gifts' -- counted as one
Rav Chisda: this baraita misled Chiyya bar Rav
ולא היא! אטו מורם מתודה ואיל נזיר דקא חשיב להו כחדא, משום דחדא נינהו? -- counting as one shows likeness, not unity
[Chiyya bar Rav, as Rav Chisda reports him]: since [the baraita] counts the gifts as one, they are one
תא שמע: one who buys the shearing of a gentile's flock is exempt from first-shearing, and this is a stringency of foreleg, jaw and maw over first-shearing -- שמע מינה בתר חיובא אזלינן
the baraita: a gentile or a priest who gave their flock to an Israelite to shear -- exempt
אלא הכא במאי עסקינן -- the gentile sits at the cash box [so the baraita need not mark]
דכוותה גבי כהן דיתיב אכספתא -- אמאי צריך לרשום? correspondingly a priest at the cash box -- why must one mark?
אמרי: המוני הימניה -- they say: he trusted him
גוי נמי אמרי: המוני הימניה -- of the gentile too they will say: he trusted him
rather, here we deal with a gentile sitting at the cash box
איבעית אימא: an ordinary gentile shouts [so his partnership is evident]
אין אמונה בגוי -- there is no trust in a gentile
there is no trust [placed] in a gentile
דכוותה גבי כהן דיתיב אמסחתא -- אמאי צריך לרשום? correspondingly a priest sitting in the shop -- why must one mark?
דאמרי: בשרא קא זבין -- they say he is buying meat
אי הכי, גוי נמי אמרי: בשרא קא זבין -- if so, of the gentile too they will say he is buying meat
[of a priest sitting in the shop] they say: he is buying meat
אמר מר: disqualified consecrated animals need not mark -- אלמא מוכחא מילתא, so the matter is evident? והא אנן תנן: they are sold, slaughtered and weighed in the market
the mishna: disqualified consecrated animals are sold in the market, slaughtered in the market, and weighed by the litra
תרגמא רב אדא בר אהבה קמיה דרב פפא: [the baraita speaks of] those sold inside the house
Rav Adda bar Ahava: [the baraita speaks of] those that are sold inside the house
מיתיבי: 'the head is mine and all of it yours' -- exempt; מאי לאו exempt from the jaw and liable in all the rest (133b.9)?
the baraita: 'the head is mine and all of it yours' -- even one-hundredth of the head -- exempt; so the foreleg, so the innards
לא, פטור מכולן -- no: exempt from all of them
no: [the baraita's 'exempt' means] exempt from all of them
וליתני פטור מכולן! -- then let it teach 'exempt from all of them'
ועוד, תניא: ... even one-hundredth of the head -- exempt from the jaw and liable in all the rest
the second baraita: 'the head is mine and all of it yours' -- even one-hundredth of the head -- exempt from the jaw and liable in all the rest
here [in the baraita] we deal with a gentile sitting in the shop
Rav Huna: a partner in the head is exempt from the jaw, a partner in the foreleg is exempt from the foreleg, a partner in the innards is exempt from the maw
whoever fulfils them is as if he fulfilled [what was given] by general statement, detail and covenant of salt; whoever transgresses them, as if he transgressed it

ten in the Temple: the sin-offering, the bird sin-offering, the certain guilt-offering, the suspended guilt-offering, the communal peace-offerings, the leper's log of oil, the two loaves, the showbread, the meal-offering remainders, and the omer meal-offering
four in Jerusalem: the firstborn, the first fruits, what is separated from the thanks-offering and from the nazir's ram, and the hides of offerings

ten in the outlying regions: teruma, teruma of the tithe, challa, first-shearing, the gifts, redemption of the son, redemption of the firstling donkey, an ancestral field, a dedicated field, and the stolen property of a convert
'the head is yours and all of it mine' -- what is [the law]? do we follow the obligation, and the obligation is with the Israelite, or the main body of the animal, which is the priest's?
the baraita: and this is a stringency in the foreleg, jaw and maw over first-shearing
